# 12-Week Upper-Body Strength Programme

**Client profile:** 29F, recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, 4 months post-physio, cleared for pain-free ROM only, no overhead loading.

**Programme goals:** Restore scapulohumeral control, rebuild pulling and pressing capacity below shoulder height, reintroduce climbing-specific demands (grip, shoulder endurance, anti-rotation), and return her to a base from which overhead work can later be reintroduced once cleared.

**Training frequency:** 3 upper-body sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri suggested), 60–75 min each. Assume she trains lower body and climbs separately under your guidance.

**Universal rules across all 12 weeks:**
- All pressing horizontal or lower; absolutely no overhead loading until medically re-cleared.
- Every session opens with 8–10 min of shoulder prep: band pull-aparts (2×15), prone Y-T-W (2×10 each), serratus wall slides below 90° (2×10), thoracic openers on foam roller.
- RPE-based loading; cap working sets at RPE 7 for first 6 weeks, RPE 8 thereafter.
- "Pain-free ROM only" — if any movement provokes the impingement arc (roughly 70–120° abduction), shorten ROM or substitute.
- Bilateral work where possible early; unilateral introduced progressively to address right-side deficit.
- Tempo notation: eccentric-pause-concentric (e.g., 3-1-1).

---

## Phase 1 — Reintegration & Scapular Control (Weeks 1–4)

**Aim:** Re-groove pain-free patterns, build scapular and rotator cuff endurance, establish baseline strength on safe ranges.

### Week 1

**Session A — Horizontal Push/Pull Foundations**
- Chest-supported row, neutral grip — 3×12 @ RPE 6, tempo 2-1-2
- Floor press, dumbbell, neutral grip — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Half-kneeling cable row, single arm — 3×12/side
- Side-lying external rotation, light DB — 3×15/side
- Pallof press — 3×10/side
- Dead hang (feet supported if needed) — 3× 15–20s

**Session B — Pulling & Cuff Endurance**
- Lat pulldown, neutral grip, sternum to bar — 3×12 @ RPE 6
- Seated cable row, wide neutral — 3×12
- Incline DB press (30°), neutral grip — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Prone trap raise (Y) on bench — 3×12
- Banded face pull (low to high, elbows below shoulder) — 3×15
- Farmer carry — 3× 30m

**Session C — Unilateral & Climbing Bias**
- Single-arm landmine press (low angle, ~45°) — 3×10/side @ RPE 6
- Single-arm cable row, half-kneeling — 3×12/side
- Push-up, hands elevated — 3×8 with scap protraction hold at top
- Bottoms-up KB carry — 3× 20m/side
- Wrist curls + reverse wrist curls — 2×15 each
- Hollow body hold — 3×20s

### Weeks 2–4 progression
- Week 2: add one set to main lifts (3→4 on row and floor press).
- Week 3: increase load so working sets sit at RPE 7; tempo eccentrics held at 3-1-1.
- Week 4: deload — drop volume 40%, keep intensity moderate; reassess pain-free ROM with the client.

By end of Phase 1 she should tolerate a heavy-ish 8-rep bench-height press and a 10-rep row without symptom reproduction.

---

## Phase 2 — Strength Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)

**Aim:** Build pulling strength (priority for climbing), introduce barbell pressing within safe ranges, deepen unilateral capacity, increase grip work.

### Week 5

**Session A — Pull-Focused**
- Weighted chin-up (or lat pulldown if bodyweight not yet ready) — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Pendlay row (or chest-supported barbell row if torso position aggravates) — 4×8
- Low-incline DB bench press (15–20°), neutral grip — 3×8
- Half-kneeling single-arm cable row — 3×10/side
- Prone Y-T-W complex — 2×8 each
- Hangboard: large edge, 7-sec hangs × 5, 3-min rest (if climbing-cleared)

**Session B — Press-Focused (Sub-shoulder)**
- Close-grip bench press — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Single-arm landmine press, standing — 4×8/side
- Chest-supported T-bar row — 3×10
- Cable face pull, tall kneeling — 3×15
- Side-lying ER + prone horizontal abduction superset — 3×12 each
- Pallof press iso hold — 3×20s/side

**Session C — Unilateral Strength & Carries**
- Single-arm DB floor press — 4×8/side
- Meadows row or single-arm DB row — 4×10/side
- Push-up variations (deficit, tempo) — 3×10
- Heavy farmer carry — 4× 30m
- Wrist roller — 3× one round up/down
- Side plank w/ row — 3×8/side

### Weeks 6–8 progression
- Week 6: linear load increase 2.5–5% on barbell lifts; sets at RPE 7–8.
- Week 7: introduce one top set + back-off sets on chin-up and close-grip bench (e.g., 1×4 @ RPE 8, then 3×6 @ RPE 7).
- Week 8: deload — halve sets on main lifts, keep cuff and scapular work full volume; check ROM and tolerance for any approach to shoulder-height pressing.

Reassess at end of Phase 2: if symptom-free and physio agrees, you can begin probing low-incline (30°) pressing more aggressively, but **still no overhead** unless re-cleared.

---

## Phase 3 — Climbing Transfer & Robustness (Weeks 9–12)

**Aim:** Bias the programme toward climbing-specific outputs — contact strength, pulling power, shoulder stability under fatigue, anti-rotation. Maintain strength gains, raise work capacity.

### Week 9

**Session A — Pulling Power**
- Weighted pull-up (mixed grips, avoid wide-grip if symptomatic) — 5×4 @ RPE 7
- Pendlay row — 4×6 @ RPE 8
- Incline DB press (30°), neutral grip — 4×8
- Single-arm half-kneeling cable row, slow eccentric — 3×8/side
- Banded external rotation at 90° abduction (below the painful arc — keep elbow at ~60°) — 3×15
- Hangboard repeaters: 7s on / 3s off × 6, ×3 sets

**Session B — Press & Stability**
- Close-grip bench press — 4×5 @ RPE 8
- Single-arm landmine press — 4×6/side
- Chest-supported row, pause at top — 4×8
- Push-up plus (scap protraction) — 3×12
- Cuban press (light, kept below shoulder) or prone W — 3×10
- Pallof press with rotation walk-out — 3×8/side

**Session C — Climbing Transfer**
- Frenchies on rings or bar (only if pull-ups symptom-free; limit hold positions to below chin) — 3× one set
- Single-arm DB row, heavy — 4×6/side
- Ring or TRX inverted row, feet elevated — 3× AMRAP-2
- Campus-style pull-up (controlled, no overhead reach) — 3×5 (or weighted pull-up cluster)
- Heavy farmer carry — 4× 40m
- Hangboard: max hang, half-crimp, 10s × 4–5 sets

### Weeks 10–12 progression
- Week 10: push top sets to RPE 8–8.5; introduce a heavy 3-rep on pull-up and close-grip bench.
- Week 11: peak week — 1×3 @ RPE 8.5 on chin-up and bench, supported by 2–3 back-off sets at RPE 7. Hangboard at full intensity for her.
- Week 12: taper — reduce volume 40%, maintain intensity Mon, easy session Wed, retest Fri.

**Week 12 retests:**
- Max weighted chin-up (5RM)
- Close-grip bench 5RM
- Single-arm DB row 8RM/side
- Max hang on chosen edge
- Subjective: pain-free ROM, sleep, end-range pressing tolerance.

---

## Recovery & Nutrition Notes (as requested in general)

If she wants guidance:
- Protein target ~1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight daily, distributed over 3–4 meals.
- Sleep 8 hrs prioritised, especially in Phases 2 and 3.
- One full rest day between upper sessions; climbing on a non-strength day, ideally with at least 24 hours' separation from the heaviest pulling session.
- Soft tissue: daily 5-min routine on pec minor, infraspinatus, lats; avoid aggressive subacromial work.
- Flag any return of night pain or painful arc immediately — that's the trigger to deload or revisit physio.

---

## Programme reintroduction notes for after Week 12

Once her physio formally clears overhead loading, spend 2–3 weeks reintroducing it with landmine press progressing to high-incline DB, then to half-kneeling overhead, before barbell pressing overhead. Don't skip steps — climbers re-aggravate impingements by jumping straight back to pull-ups with full overhead reach plus pressing in the same week.

Let me know her current bodyweight pull-up and bench numbers and I'll plug specific loads into Phase 1, Week 1.

# Nutrition Plan — Body Recomposition Focus

To complement the 12-week upper-body programme. Assumes she's training upper body 3×/week, climbing 1–2×/week, plus lower-body work — call it 5 training days, 2 rest days.

**Caveat:** I don't have her bodyweight, height, or body composition, so I'll build this around a working assumption of 60 kg, ~25% body fat, moderately active outside the gym. Scale linearly — I've noted where.

---

## Strategy Overview

Body recomposition (simultaneous fat loss and muscle gain) works best for someone who is:
- Returning to structured training after a layoff (✓ she is, due to the injury)
- Not yet near her strength ceiling (✓)
- Willing to eat at maintenance or a *small* deficit while hitting high protein

So the approach is: **slight calorie deficit (~10–15%), high protein, calorie cycling around training days, and patience.** Aggressive deficits will blunt her strength rebuild and slow tendon/cuff adaptation — important given the impingement history.

---

## Calorie & Macro Targets

**Estimated maintenance:** ~2,100 kcal/day (60 kg × ~35 kcal/kg given training load).

**Target intake:**
- **Training days:** ~2,000 kcal
- **Rest days:** ~1,750 kcal
- **Weekly average:** ~1,930 kcal (≈8% deficit — gentle, sustainable)

**Macros (daily averages):**
| Macro | Grams | kcal | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| Protein | 120 g (2.0 g/kg) | 480 | 25% |
| Fat | 65 g (~1.1 g/kg) | 585 | 30% |
| Carbs | 215 g (~3.6 g/kg) | 860 | 45% |

**Carb cycling:**
- Training days: 240 g carbs / 55 g fat
- Rest days: 175 g carbs / 70 g fat
- Protein stays at 120 g every day — non-negotiable.

**Scaling:** if she's not 60 kg, multiply protein at 2.0 g/kg, fat at 1.0–1.2 g/kg, and calculate calories at ~32 kcal/kg (rest) and ~36 kcal/kg (training). Carbs fill the remainder.

---

## Meal Structure

Four feedings/day works well for her schedule and protein distribution (~30 g protein per meal saturates muscle protein synthesis).

### Training day template (~2,000 kcal)

**Breakfast (~500 kcal)**
- 3 whole eggs + 100 g egg whites scrambled
- 60 g oats with 100 g berries
- Black coffee
- *~35 g P / 50 g C / 18 g F*

**Pre-training meal, ~90 min before (~450 kcal)**
- 150 g chicken breast
- 80 g (dry) rice or 250 g cooked sweet potato
- Mixed veg, 1 tsp olive oil
- *~40 g P / 65 g C / 10 g F*

**Post-training (~500 kcal)**
- Whey protein shake (30 g)
- 1 banana + 1 slice sourdough with honey
- Greek yogurt (150 g, 0–2% fat)
- *~45 g P / 75 g C / 5 g F*

**Dinner (~550 kcal)**
- 150 g salmon or 180 g lean beef
- Large salad with 1 tbsp olive oil + vinegar
- 200 g roasted veg, small portion of grain (~40 g dry)
- *~40 g P / 50 g C / 22 g F*

### Rest day template (~1,750 kcal)

Same structure, but:
- Drop pre-training meal's carbs by ~30 g (smaller rice portion)
- Drop post-workout shake; replace with cottage cheese (200 g) + handful of nuts
- Add a small handful of almonds or avocado at dinner for satiety
- *Net effect: ~250 fewer kcal, mostly from carbs, slight fat increase*

---

## Phase-Specific Adjustments

The programme's demands change across 12 weeks, so should her intake.

### Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Reintegration
- Sit at the calorie targets above.
- **Priority:** protein consistency, not deficit aggression. She's rebuilding tissue tolerance — under-fuelling here slows tendon and cuff adaptation.
- Expect 0.3–0.5 kg fat loss/week, possible scale weight stability if muscle is accruing.

### Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength accumulation
- Training intensity rises — **add 25–30 g carbs to training-day pre and post meals** (≈+200 kcal on training days only).
- Rest days unchanged.
- This widens the carb cycle and supports the heavier pulling work without compromising the weekly deficit much.

### Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Climbing transfer & peak
- Hangboarding and high-output pulling are glycolytic and CNS-demanding.
- **Move to maintenance on training days** (~2,150 kcal), keep rest days at 1,750.
- Weekly deficit shrinks to ~5%, but performance and recovery take priority during the peaking block.

# Hangboard & Climbing-Specific Prep — Phases 2 & 3

The earlier programme included light hangboard mentions; this expands them into a structured progression. Climbing-specific finger and shoulder loading is where her impingement history demands the most care — the dead-hang position itself can provoke symptoms if scapular control fails or grip positions force the humerus into impingement range.

---

## Guiding Principles

1. **No hangboarding in Phase 1.** Four months post-physio with no overhead loading clearance means dead hangs — which are essentially passive overhead loading — are off the table until she's demonstrated scapular control and pain-free pressing at shoulder height. Phase 1 builds that foundation.
2. **Active hangs before passive hangs.** She must own the "shoulders engaged, scaps depressed and slightly retracted" position before any passive bar hang is introduced.
3. **Half-crimp only for max hangs through Week 10.** Full crimp is loaded later and only if symptom-free; open hand is fine throughout.
4. **No campusing, no dynos, no full-crimp limit work in this block.** Save for post-programme.
5. **Sequence within a session:** finger work *before* fatigue. Hangboard goes at the start of the session, after warm-up, before pulling.
6. **Stop rules:** any shoulder symptom reproduction, any finger pain beyond mild discomfort, any pop or sharp sensation — session ends. Non-negotiable.

# Mobility Programme — Integrated Across 12 Weeks

Mobility for this client serves three jobs:
1. **Preserve and expand pain-free shoulder ROM** as she progresses through rehab
2. **Address climber-typical restrictions** — thoracic spine, hips, pec minor, lats
3. **Support the eventual return to overhead loading** by keeping the tissues that *gate* overhead access (lats, pec minor, thoracic extension) supple and functional

This isn't a generic stretching routine bolted on the side. It's prescribed by phase, with daily, pre-session, and dedicated session components.

---

## Climber-Specific Restrictions to Target

Most climbers — and her medical history compounds this — present with:
- **Pec minor and anterior shoulder tightness** (chronic flexion-dominant sport)
- **Thoracic kyphosis and limited T-spine extension/rotation** (forearm flexion bias, hunched posture under load)
- **Tight lats** (overhead reach pattern repeated thousands of times)
- **Internal rotation dominance, weak external rotation** (the impingement substrate)
- **Hip flexor and adductor tightness** (high-step and stem positions)
- **Limited ankle dorsiflexion** (heel hooks, edging)
- **Forearm flexor tightness** (obvious, but often neglected)

For her specifically, **pec minor + lats + thoracic extension** are the top three. These three together gate her future overhead clearance — keeping them mobile during this block sets her up for a faster overhead reintroduction post-Week 12.

## Specific Movements — Form Notes

For the trainer to cue her on. These are the high-value movements and the ones most likely to be done wrong.

**Doorway pec stretch:**
- Elbow at 90°, forearm flat against frame
- Step the same-side foot forward, rotate torso *away* from the arm
- Three angles: forearm low (~60° abduction), mid (~90°), high (~120°). **Skip the high angle in Phase 1**, introduce gently Phase 2, normal use Phase 3.
- She should feel it across the anterior chest — *not* into the front of the shoulder joint. Sharp anterior shoulder = back off.

**Lat stretch (kneeling on bench):**
- Hands shoulder-width on bench or bar
- Sit hips back toward heels
- Drop chest toward floor
- Keep arms straight, breathe into the lats
- **Do not let the lumbar spine extend** — she should feel a stretch along the side body, not in her lower back

**Thoracic extension on foam roller:**
- Roller perpendicular to spine, mid-back
- Hands behind head supporting neck
- Extend backward over roller, exhale, return
- Move the roller up an inch, repeat. Cover from mid-back to T6.
- **Do not roll cervical or lumbar spine.**

**Open book stretch:**
- Side-lying, knees bent stacked, top arm out at 90°
- Sweep top arm across body in big arc, follow with eyes
- Try to land top shoulder flat to floor
- Hold 2 breaths at end range
- Right side will lag — work it patiently

**Sleeper stretch:**
- Side-lying on affected side, elbow under shoulder, forearm up
- Other hand gently presses forearm toward floor (internal rotation)
- **Gentle pressure only** — this position can aggravate impingement if forced
- Skip entirely if anterior shoulder symptom; substitute with a different posterior capsule mobilisation

## Red Flags — When Mobility Becomes the Problem

Mobility work for a rehabbing shoulder can do harm if pushed wrong. Stop and reassess if:
- Sharp anterior shoulder pain during any stretch (especially pec stretches at high arm angles)
- Tingling or numbness in the arm or hand (possible neurological irritation)
- Stretch sensation that doesn't release after 30 s (muscle is guarding, force won't help)
- Soreness in the shoulder joint capsule lasting >24 hr post-session
- Loss of strength in the days following a mobility session (over-mobilisation)

**Bias toward strengthening through range rather than passively stretching to range.** The CARs, controlled extensions, and end-range loading patterns are the durable adaptations. Passive stretches are supplementary.

# Complete 12-Week Programme — Final Consolidated Version

**Client:** 29F, recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, 4 months post-physio, cleared for pain-free ROM only, no overhead loading.

**Targets:**
1. Restore pain-free upper-body strength and scapulohumeral control
2. Body recomposition (Phases 1–2), shifting to performance fuelling (Phase 3)
3. Build aerobic base and approach-day fitness
4. Reintroduce hangboarding and climbing-specific demands
5. **Peak for a climbing trip starting Week 12**

**Working assumptions:** 60 kg bodyweight (scale nutrition linearly), 5 training days, 1 rest day, 1 climbing day. Full gym access.

## Universal Rules (Apply Throughout)

- No overhead loading until medically re-cleared
- All work in pain-free ROM only — any impingement arc symptom = stop, reassess, modify
- Tempo notation: eccentric-pause-concentric (e.g., 3-1-1)
- RPE caps: ≤7 in Phase 1, ≤8 in Phase 2, up to 9 in Phase 3 peak
- Every session opens with 8–10 min shoulder prep: band pull-aparts (2×15), prone Y-T-W (2×10 each), serratus wall slides below 90° (2×10), thoracic openers on roller
- Daily 10-min mobility routine (every day, every phase — see Mobility section)
- Stop rules: any shoulder symptom recurrence, sharp finger pain, elbow pain, sleep disruption, or resting HR up 7+ bpm for 2+ days = pull back

- Chest-supported row, neutral grip — 3×12 @ RPE 6, tempo 2-1-2

- **Week 3:** loads to RPE 7, tempo eccentrics at 3-1-1

**Daily 10-min routine (all 12 weeks):** cat-cow 1 min, world's greatest stretch 5/side, T-spine on roller 1 min, doorway pec stretch 30 s/side × 2 (low/mid angles only this phase), lat stretch 45 s × 2, half-kneeling hip flexor + cleared-ROM reach 30 s/side × 2, wrist flow 1 min.

- Push-up variations (deficit, tempo) — 3×10

- Wrist roller — 3 × one round up/down

### Week-by-week loading
- **Week 6:** linear load increase 2.5–5% on barbell lifts; working sets RPE 7–8

- Pain-free 15 s active hang

# Complete 12-Week Programme — Final Consolidated Version

**Client:** 29F, recreational climber, right subacromial impingement, 4 months post-physio, cleared for pain-free ROM only, no overhead loading.

**Targets:**
1. Restore pain-free upper-body strength and scapulohumeral control
2. Body recomposition (Phases 1–2), shifting to performance fuelling (Phase 3)
3. Build aerobic base and approach-day fitness
4. Reintroduce hangboarding and climbing-specific demands
5. **Peak for a climbing trip starting Week 12**

**Working assumptions:** 60 kg bodyweight (scale nutrition linearly), 5 training days, 1 rest day, 1 climbing day. Full gym access.

---

## Universal Rules (Apply Throughout)

- No overhead loading until medically re-cleared
- All work in pain-free ROM only — any impingement arc symptom = stop, reassess, modify
- Tempo notation: eccentric-pause-concentric (e.g., 3-1-1)
- RPE caps: ≤7 in Phase 1, ≤8 in Phase 2, up to 9 in Phase 3 peak
- Every session opens with 8–10 min shoulder prep: band pull-aparts (2×15), prone Y-T-W (2×10 each), serratus wall slides below 90° (2×10), thoracic openers on roller
- Daily 10-min mobility routine (every day, every phase — see Mobility section)
- Stop rules: any shoulder symptom recurrence, sharp finger pain, elbow pain, sleep disruption, or resting HR up 7+ bpm for 2+ days = pull back

---

# PHASE 1 — REINTEGRATION & SCAPULAR CONTROL (Weeks 1–4)

**Aim:** Re-groove pain-free patterns, build cuff and scapular endurance, establish strength baseline, build aerobic base.

## Weekly Schedule

| Day | Session | Approx. Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Upper A | 60 min |
| Tue | Lower + Z2 cardio + dedicated mobility | 90 min |
| Wed | Upper B | 60 min |
| Thu | Climbing day | 60–75 min |
| Fri | Upper C | 60 min |
| Sat | Hike + circuit + finisher | 60–90 min |
| Sun | Dedicated mobility + rest | 25 min |

## Strength Sessions

### Session A — Horizontal Push/Pull Foundations
- Chest-supported row, neutral grip — 3×12 @ RPE 6, tempo 2-1-2
- Floor press, DB neutral grip — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Half-kneeling cable row, single arm — 3×12/side
- Side-lying external rotation, light DB — 3×15/side
- Pallof press — 3×10/side
- Dead hang (feet supported) — 3 × 15–20 s

### Session B — Pulling & Cuff Endurance
- Lat pulldown, neutral grip, sternum to bar — 3×12 @ RPE 6
- Seated cable row, wide neutral — 3×12
- Incline DB press (30°), neutral grip — 3×10 @ RPE 6
- Prone trap raise (Y) on bench — 3×12
- Banded face pull (low to high, elbows below shoulder) — 3×15
- Farmer carry — 3 × 30 m

### Session C — Unilateral & Climbing Bias
- Single-arm landmine press (~45° angle) — 3×10/side @ RPE 6
- Single-arm cable row, half-kneeling — 3×12/side
- Push-up, hands elevated, scap protraction hold at top — 3×8
- Bottoms-up KB carry — 3 × 20 m/side
- Wrist curls + reverse wrist curls — 2×15 each
- Hollow body hold — 3 × 20 s

### Week-by-week loading
- **Week 1:** as above
- **Week 2:** add one set to main rows and presses (3→4)
- **Week 3:** loads to RPE 7, tempo eccentrics at 3-1-1
- **Week 4:** deload — volume −40%, intensity moderate; reassess pain-free ROM

## Cardio (2×/week)

**Tuesday — Zone 2 steady state, bike or incline walk (8–12% gradient, no running)**
- Wk 1: 30 min / Wk 2: 35 min / Wk 3: 40 min / Wk 4: 30 min (deload)

**Saturday hike (part of Saturday day, see below)**

**HR zones (max ~191):** Z2 = 124–143 bpm; nasal breathing where possible.

## Climbing — Thursday

- Warm-up: 15 min easy traversing, progressive route grades
- Main: 45–60 min route climbing, 2–3 grades below redpoint
- No bouldering above moderate intensity, technique focus
- Cool-down: shoulder mobility, finger extensions
- **No hangboarding this phase.**

## Saturday Day

- **Block 1 — Hike:** Wk 1: 45 min, no pack / Wk 2: 50 min, no pack / Wk 3: 60 min, 3 kg / Wk 4: 40 min, no pack
- **Block 2 — Circuit (2 rounds):** goblet squat 10, push-up (hands elevated if needed) 8, single-arm DB row 10/side, farmer carry 30 m, dead bug 8/side
- **Block 3 — Fun finisher (rotate):** Wk 1 sled push+pull 4×20 m / Wk 2 battle ropes 5 × 30 s on / 60 s off / Wk 3 med ball slams (sub-shoulder release) + goblet squat 6 rounds of 5+5 / Wk 4 easy bike + carry medley × 3
- **Block 4 — Cool-down:** 5 min world's greatest stretch, doorway pec, lat stretch

## Mobility — Phase 1

**Daily 10-min routine (all 12 weeks):** cat-cow 1 min, world's greatest stretch 5/side, T-spine on roller 1 min, doorway pec stretch 30 s/side × 2 (low/mid angles only this phase), lat stretch 45 s × 2, half-kneeling hip flexor + cleared-ROM reach 30 s/side × 2, wrist flow 1 min.

**Pre-session prep (5–8 min before every gym/climb session):** foam roll T-spine 90 s + lats 30 s/side, quadruped T-rotation 8/side, wall slides at 60° abduction 2×8, banded shoulder distraction in cleared ROM 30 s/side.

**Tuesday dedicated session (25 min) — full body recovery:** foam roll lower body 5 min, 90/90 hip switches 10/side × 2, half-kneeling adductor rock-back 8/side × 2, couch stretch 60 s/side × 2, quadruped T-rotation 10/side × 2, child's pose with low lat reach 60 s × 2, supine pec stretch over roller (arms at 60° abduction) 2 min, diaphragmatic breathing 10 breaths.

**Sunday dedicated session (25 min) — upper bias:** foam roll T-spine + lats + pecs 5 min, T-extension over roller 8 reps × 2, open book 8/side × 2, doorway pec stretch low/mid angles 30 s × 2 × 2 sides, lat stretch quadruped 60 s × 3, sleeper stretch gentle 30 s/side × 2, wrist flow 3 min, cervical mobility 2 min.

**Phase 1 mobility goal:** pain-free T-extension over roller; pain-free lat stretch in quadruped, no anterior pinch.

## Nutrition — Phase 1

Estimated maintenance ~2,100 kcal (60 kg × ~35 kcal/kg).

**Daily protein:** 120 g (2.0 g/kg) — non-negotiable, ~30 g × 4 meals.

| Day type | Calories | Carbs | Protein | Fat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Training day (Mon/Wed/Fri/Tue/Thu) | 2,000 | 240 g | 120 g | 55 g |
| Saturday | 1,850 | 200 g | 120 g | 65 g |
| Sunday (rest) | 1,750 | 175 g | 120 g | 70 g |

**Weekly average:** ~1,930 kcal (≈8% deficit).

**Training day meal template:**
- Breakfast (~500 kcal): 3 whole eggs + 100 g egg whites, 60 g oats with 100 g berries, black coffee
- Pre-training (~450 kcal): 150 g chicken, 80 g (dry) rice or 250 g sweet potato, mixed veg + 1 tsp olive oil
- Post-training (~500 kcal): 30 g whey, 1 banana + 1 slice sourdough + honey, 150 g Greek yogurt
- Dinner (~550 kcal): 150 g salmon or 180 g lean beef, large salad + 1 tbsp olive oil, 200 g roasted veg + ~40 g (dry) grain

**Rest day:** drop pre-training meal's carbs by ~30 g, drop the post-workout shake (sub cottage cheese 200 g + handful of nuts), add small handful nuts/avocado at dinner.

**Supplements:** Creatine 5 g/day, Vitamin D3 1,000–2,000 IU/day, Omega-3 2 g EPA/DHA/day, collagen 15 g + 50 mg vit C 45–60 min pre-cuff/shoulder work (Phase 1–2), whey as needed.

**Hydration:** 2.5–3 L/day, more on climbing days. 500–800 mg sodium pre-training if she sweats heavily.

---

# PHASE 2 — STRENGTH ACCUMULATION (Weeks 5–8)

**Aim:** Build pulling strength, introduce barbell pressing within safe range, deepen unilateral capacity, reintroduce hangboard, raise cardio capacity.

## Strength Sessions

### Session A — Pull-Focused
- Weighted chin-up (or lat pulldown if not yet ready) — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Pendlay row (or chest-supported barbell row) — 4×8
- Low-incline DB bench press (15–20°), neutral grip — 3×8
- Half-kneeling single-arm cable row — 3×10/side
- Prone Y-T-W complex — 2×8 each
- **Hangboard (from Week 5) at start of session — see Hangboard block below**

### Session B — Press-Focused (Sub-Shoulder)
- Close-grip bench press — 4×6 @ RPE 7
- Single-arm landmine press, standing — 4×8/side
- Chest-supported T-bar row — 3×10
- Cable face pull, tall kneeling — 3×15
- Side-lying ER + prone horizontal abduction superset — 3×12 each
- Pallof press iso hold — 3 × 20 s/side

### Session C — Unilateral Strength & Carries
- Single-arm DB floor press — 4×8/side
- Meadows row or single-arm DB row — 4×10/side
- Push-up variations (deficit, tempo) — 3×10
- Heavy farmer carry — 4 × 30 m
- Wrist roller — 3 × one round up/down
- Side plank with row — 3×8/side

### Week-by-week loading
- **Week 6:** linear load increase 2.5–5% on barbell lifts; working sets RPE 7–8
- **Week 7:** introduce top set + back-off on chin-up and close-grip bench (1×4 @ RPE 8, then 3×6 @ RPE 7)
- **Week 8:** deload — main lifts at half volume, cuff/scap work full volume; reassess for any approach to shoulder-height pressing

## Hangboard — Phase 2 Reintroduction

Placed at start of **Wednesday (Session B)** after warm-up.

**Universal pre-hangboard warm-up (~8 min):** band finger extensions 2×20, rice bucket/putty 2 × 30 s, easy traversing or jug hangs (feet on) 3 min, progressive edge loading 20 mm @ 50% BW × 3 × 7 s, scap pull-ups 5 + serratus push-ups 8.

- **Week 5:** Active scap hangs (jug/large rung), 5 × 10 s, 2 min rest. + 20-mm half-crimp with feet partially on stool (~30% offload), 5 × 7 s, 3 min rest.
- **Week 6:** Active hangs 5 × 12 s, 2 min rest. 20-mm half-crimp at bodyweight if Wk 5 clean, 5 × 7 s, 3 min rest. If shoulders flag, 15% offload.
- **Week 7:** Active hangs 5 × 15 s. 20-mm half-crimp +2.5 kg if Wk 6 clean, 5 × 7 s. Open-hand on same edge, 3 × 7 s BW.
- **Week 8 deload:** Active hangs 3 × 10 s. 20-mm half-crimp BW only, 3 × 7 s. Skip open-hand.

**End-of-Phase-2 checkpoints before progressing:**
- Pain-free 15 s active hang
- Pain-free 7 s half-crimp BW on 20 mm
- No shoulder symptoms during or 24 hr after ARC
- Close-grip bench @ RPE 8 without shoulder reaction
- Weighted chin-up @ RPE 8 without shoulder reaction
- If any fail → repeat Wk 7 instead of progressing

## Cardio — Phase 2

**Tuesday — Extended Z2 (bike preferred):**
Wk 5: 45 min / Wk 6: 50 min / Wk 7: 55 min / Wk 8: 35 min

**Saturday hike (part of Saturday day below)**

**Threshold intervals fold into Saturday's finisher when appropriate (see below).**

## Climbing — Thursday

- Warm-up: 15 min progressive grades
- Main: 45–60 min routes at 2–3 grades below redpoint
- ARC: Wk 5 — 2 × 10 min, 5 min rest; Wk 6 — 2 × 12 min; Wk 7 — 3 × 10 min; Wk 8 — 1 × 15 min easy
- Cool-down: shoulder mobility, finger extensions

## Climbing-Specific Shoulder Work (added to gym sessions Phase 2)

- **Scapular pull-ups** — 3 × 8, in Wednesday warm-up
- **TRX/ring rows with offset grip** — 3×8/side, Friday
- **Half-kneeling cable pull-down to chest** (not overhead) — 3×10/side, Friday

## Saturday Day — Phase 2

**Block 1 — Hike:** Wk 5: 60 min, 5 kg / Wk 6: 70 min, 6 kg / Wk 7: 75 min, 7 kg / Wk 8: 50 min, 4 kg (deload)

**Block 2 — Circuit (2 rounds):** KB swing 12, push-up full ROM controlled 10, TRX/ring row 10, suitcase carry 30 m/side, hollow hold 20 s. RPE 6–7, 90 s rest.

**Block 3 — Finisher (rotate):**
- Wk 5: heavy bear-hug carries 4 × 30 m (skip shoulder carries)
- Wk 6: bouldering wall play — 20 min easy traversing, sea-level, no power moves
- Wk 7: sled medley — push 20 m, drag back 20 m, lateral drag 20 m/side, 3 rounds
- Wk 8: bike intervals 6 × 30 s hard / 90 s easy (deload week)

**Threshold work option:** If she wants the Phase 2 cardio plan's threshold intervals (4×4 min Z4) instead of the finisher rotation, run them weeks 5–7 only on Saturday, not in addition to. Most clients prefer the variety route — pick one.

**Block 4 — Cool-down:** 5 min doorway pec, lat stretch, T-spine on roller, hip flexor.

## Mobility — Phase 2

**Daily routine and pre-session prep:** unchanged from Phase 1, but doorway pec stretch now uses **low/mid/high angles** (introduce high cautiously).

**Tuesday dedicated session (28 min):** Phase 1 routine + shoulder CARs 3 reps/direction/side in cleared ROM + lizard pose with rotation 5/side × 2 + cossack squat hold 30 s/side × 2.

**Sunday dedicated session (30 min):** Phase 1 routine + banded lat distraction 60 s/side × 2 + pec minor release with lacrosse ball 90 s/side + T-extension on roller loaded (5 kg plate) 6 × 2 + prone scorpion gentle 6/side × 2 + PAILs/RAILs at 90° flexion 2 cycles/side (if comfortable with technique) + sleeper stretch progression 45 s/side × 2.
